In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment

 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

214	### 4.4 Ignite:用 Engine 保留循环、用回调拼装行为
215	
216	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
217	
218	Ignite 与 Lightning 的哲学不同。Lightning 把循环**藏起来**(你只写 step);Ignite 把循环**封装但保持可见**——核心类 `Engine` 接收一个「处理单个 batch 的函数」,替你跑双层循环并在各个时点触发事件,你再用回调把日志、验证、存档挂上去。书中源码注释([ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L70-L79](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L70-L79))总结为四件套:引擎与事件系统、开箱即用指标、内置 handlers、分布式支持。设计取向是「比纯 PyTorch 少写代码,但保留 PyTorch 式的完全控制」。
219	
220	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
221	
222	数据与模型准备仍是纯 PyTorch(见 [ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L105-L156](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L105-L156),`get_model` 函数 + 手动 `.to(device)`),然后:
223	
224	```
225	trainer = create_supervised_trainer(model, optimizer, loss_fn, device=device)   # 训练引擎
226	evaluator = create_supervised_evaluator(model, metrics={...}, device=device)    # 评估引擎
227	# 给 trainer 挂事件回调(日志、checkpoint)→ 给 evaluator 挂回调(验证指标、最佳模型)
228	trainer.run(train_loader, max_epochs=5)                                          # 一行启动
229	```
230	
231	`create_supervised_trainer` 内部的循环等价于(伪代码):
232	
233	```
234	while epoch < max_epochs:
235	    for batch in data:
236	        model.train(); x, y = move_to_device(batch)
237	        y_pred = model(x); loss = loss_fn(y_pred, y)
238	        optimizer.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); optimizer.step()
239	        触发 Events.ITERATION_COMPLETED(把 loss 存进 trainer.state.output)
240	    触发 Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED
241	触发 Events.COMPLETED
242	```
243	
244	也就是 u12-l3 的五步骨架原封不动,只是由引擎执行、并在固定时点发事件。

272	**练习 2**:与 Lightning 相比,Ignite 版里设备管理是更省心还是更操心?
273	**答案**:更操心。Ignite 版要自己写 `device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"` 并把 `device` 传给两个引擎([L152-L182](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L152-L182));Lightning 只需 Trainer 传 `gpus=1`,模块与数据的转移全部自动。
274	
275	### 4.5 Ignite 的 Events 事件系统与 handlers
276	
277	#### 4.5.1 概念说明
278	
279	`Engine` 在固定时点触发事件(事件是一个枚举 `Events`,如 `ITERATION_COMPLETED`、`EPOCH_COMPLETED`、`COMPLETED`),你把普通 Python 函数挂到事件上,它们就成了回调。挂接有两种等价写法:**装饰器** `@trainer.on(Events.XXX)` 与显式调用 `trainer.add_event_handler(Events.XXX, fn)`。此外 Ignite 内置了一类现成回调——handlers,如 `Checkpoint`(存档)、`DiskSaver`(写磁盘)、`TensorboardLogger`(写 TensorBoard),直接拿来挂即可,不必自己写函数。
280	
281	#### 4.5.2 核心流程
282	
283	```
284	@trainer.on(Events.ITERATION_COMPLETED(every=100))   # 带过滤器:每 100 个 iteration
285	def log_training_loss(): ...                          # 打印 trainer.state.output 里的 batch 损失
286	
287	@trainer.on(Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED)                   # 每个 epoch 结束
288	def log_validation_results():
289	    evaluator.run(val_loader)                          # 跑评估引擎 → 读 state.metrics
290	
291	trainer.add_event_handler(Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED, checkpoint_handler)   # 每 epoch 存档
292	evaluator.add_event_handler(Events.COMPLETED, best_model_handler)       # 每次评估后按准确率存最佳
293	tb_logger.attach_output_handler(...)                  # 指标写入 TensorBoard
294	```
295	
296	`trainer.state` 是引擎的「仪表盘」:`state.epoch`、`state.max_epochs`、`state.iteration`、`state.output`(当前 batch 的损失)在回调里随取随用。
297	
298	#### 4.5.3 源码精读
299	
300	训练日志回调:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L193-L202](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L193-L202)。`Events.ITERATION_COMPLETED(every=log_interval)` 是「事件 + 过滤器」的组合,`log_interval=100` 意味着并非每个 batch 都打印(否则 938 个 iteration/epoch 会刷屏);函数体从 `trainer.state` 取 epoch、iteration 和当前批损失并格式化打印。
301	
302	验证回调:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L212-L220](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L212-L220)。挂在 **trainer** 的 `EPOCH_COMPLETED` 上,函数体却去 `evaluator.run(val_loader)`——「训练引擎的 epoch 结束」触发「评估引擎完整跑一遍验证集」,这是两个 Engine 协作的典型写法;`eval_state.metrics['accuracy']` 与 `['loss']` 正是 4.4 建指标表时自定义的键名。
303	
304	每 epoch 存档:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L230-L242](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L230-L242)。`to_save = {"model": model, "optimizer": optimizer, "trainer": trainer}` 说明存档内容不止模型参数(与 u13-l2 的 checkpoint 概念对齐:含优化器状态才能严格续训);`DiskSaver(dirname="./output", require_empty=False)` 负责写盘;`Checkpoint(to_save, save_handler, filename_prefix="training")` 组装后用**显式** `trainer.add_event_handler(Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED, checkpoint_handler)` 挂上——源码注释 L205 特意说明这与装饰器写法等价。
305	
306	按验证准确率存最佳模型:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L253-L263](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L253-L263)。又一个 `Checkpoint`,但 `n_saved=1`、`score_name="accuracy"`、`score_function=Checkpoint.get_default_score_fn("accuracy")`(从 evaluator 的指标表里取 accuracy 打分),并且挂在 **evaluator** 的 `COMPLETED` 上——每次评估完就「以准确率为分数」覆盖式保存,与 Lightning `ModelCheckpoint(monitor="valid_acc", mode='max', save_top_k=1)` 目的相同,只是这里需要你亲手接线。
307	
308	TensorBoard 日志:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L266-L291](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L266-L291)。`TensorboardLogger(log_dir=output_path)` 之后调用两次 `attach_output_handler`:一次挂 trainer 的 `ITERATION_COMPLETED(every=100)` 写批损失(`output_transform=lambda loss: {"batch_loss": loss}` 把引擎输出变换为要记录的字典),一次挂 evaluator 的 `EPOCH_COMPLETED` 写全部指标(`metric_names="all"`),`global_step_transform=global_step_from_engine(trainer)` 让验证曲线的横坐标对齐训练引擎的全局步数而非评估引擎自己的步数——否则两条曲线在 TensorBoard 里对不齐。启动看板:`tensorboard --logdir='./output'`(源码注释 L303-L305)。
309	
310	#### 4.5.4 代码实践(本地验证型)
311	
312	1. **实践目标**:体会「回调挂接点」与「执行频率」的关系。
313	2. **操作步骤**:把 [L194](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L194) 的 `log_interval` 从 100 改为 10,运行脚本;再把 L212 的装饰器从 `Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED` 改成 `Events.ITERATION_COMPLETED(every=200)`,观察验证输出的频率变化。
314	3. **需要观察的现象**:第一步打印行数变为原来的 10 倍;第二步验证评估从每 epoch 一次变成每 200 个 iteration 一次(一个 epoch 内出现多行验证结果,且每行都要把 10000 张验证图整个跑一遍,训练明显变慢)。
315	4. **预期结果**:确认「事件决定挂接点、过滤器决定频率、评估本身有成本」三点。**待本地验证**。
316	
317	#### 4.5.5 小练习与答案
318	
319	**练习 1**:`log_training_loss` 挂在 trainer 上、`best_model_handler` 挂在 evaluator 上,为什么不能反过来?
320	**答案**:`best_model_handler` 的分数函数要从评估指标里取 accuracy,而只有 evaluator 跑完验证集后指标才就绪;挂在 trainer 的 `EPOCH_COMPLETED` 上时指标表还没更新,分数无从谈起(且那一刻 `COMPLETED` 尚未触发)。
321	
322	**练习 2**:Ignite 的 `Checkpoint(to_save={...})` 与 u13-l2 讲的 `torch.save(model.state_dict())` 有什么关系?
323	**答案**:前者是后者的自动化包装——按事件定时触发、可同时保存 model/optimizer/trainer 多个对象、还能按分数保留最佳;底层仍是把各对象的 state_dict 序列化到磁盘。
324	
325	## 5. 综合实践
326	
327	**任务:同一模型的三种训练写法对比实验。**
328	
329	> 说明:大纲原始任务写的是「把 Lightning 模型的 epoch 从 200 降到 50」。核对当前 HEAD 源码,Lightning 脚本的轮数实为 `max_epochs=10`([L208/L210](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L207-L210));「200」其实是原始 PyTorch XOR 项目的 `num_epochs=200`([ch13/ch13_part1.py:L281](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part1.py#L281))。实践按真实代码执行。
330	
331	**步骤 1(Lightning 轮数扫描)**:在 [ch13_part3_lightning.py](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py) 中把 `max_epochs` 分别设为 5、10、15 各跑一次,每次记录:(a) 进度条/日志里的 `valid_acc`;(b) `trainer.test(ckpt_path='best')` 输出的 `test_acc`;(c) checkpoints 目录里最终存档文件名中的 epoch 号。
332	
333	**步骤 2(Ignite 运行)**:安装 `pytorch-ignite`(版本 0.4.x,见源码注释 L86),运行 [ch13_part4_ignite.py](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py)(`max_epochs=5`),记录每个 epoch 打印的 `Avg Accuracy`,并检查 `./output` 目录下生成的 `training_*.ckpt` 与 `best_*.ckpt` 文件。
334	
335	**步骤 3(代码量与结构对比)**:用统一口径(只统计与「训练执行」直接相关的代码,排除数据下载与可视化)填写下表并数行数:
336	
337	| 维度 | 原始 PyTorch(part2) | Lightning(part3) | Ignite(part4) |
338	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
339	| 训练循环谁写 | 自己写(L260-L273,14 行) | 框架(`training_step` 6 行/步) | 框架(`trainer.run` 1 行启动) |
340	| 设备转移 | 无(CPU)/自己 `.to(device)` | `gpus=1` 一个参数 | 手动传 `device` 给两个引擎 |
341	| 验证集 | 无 | `random_split` 55000/5000 | 直接用测试集(源码已注明) |
342	| 指标累计 | 手写 `accuracy_hist_train` | torchmetrics 三段式 | `Accuracy`/`Loss` 指标表 |
343	| 最佳模型存档 | 无 | `ModelCheckpoint` 一行配置 | `Checkpoint` + 分数函数手动接线 |
344	
345	**步骤 4(写总结)**:用 200 字左右回答:三种写法各自的总行数是多少?在小模型场景下「行数更少」是否是选择框架的主要理由?如果不是,是什么?
346	
347	**预期结果**(待本地验证):Lightning 与 Ignite 的验证/测试准确率都应在 0.93~0.96 区间(与 u11 手写 MLP 的 94%~95% 相当,模型结构相同量级);`max_epochs` 从 5 到 15,`valid_acc` 前期上升明显、后期趋平甚至过拟合。总结的参考要点:这个规模下三种写法总行数相差不大(Lightning 甚至因类定义更多而更长),框架的真实收益在于**结构**:验证集切分、最佳模型挑选、断点续训、TensorBoard 这些「容易忘写的工程项」被标准化了;Lightning 适合想要「约定优于配置」的快速实验,Ignite 适合想要「循环可见、按事件精细控制」的场景。
348	
349	## 6. 本讲小结
350	
351	- `LightningModule` 把「单 batch 的训练/验证/测试怎么算」(`training_step` / `validation_step` / `test_step`)和「用哪个优化器」(`configure_optimizers`)收进模型类,梯度三件套(backward/step/zero_grad)全部交给 Trainer。
352	- torchmetrics 指标对象用 `update → compute → reset` 三段式累计,epoch 末得到的是按样本数加权的整体准确率,而非批准确率的平均。
353	- `LightningDataModule` 用 `prepare_data`(下载一次)/ `setup`(切分)/ 三个 `*_dataloader` 统一数据准备;它是三种实现中唯一真正切出 5000 张验证集的版本。
354	- `ModelCheckpoint(monitor="valid_acc", mode='max', save_top_k=1)` 与 `self.log` 的键名构成隐式契约;`trainer.test(ckpt_path='best')` 自动加载验证集上最优的存档。
355	- Ignite 的核心是 `Engine` + `Events`:循环被封装但仍可见,日志、验证、checkpoint、TensorBoard 全部以回调/ handler 的形式挂接到具体事件上,`trainer.run(data, max_epochs=5)` 一行启动。
356	- 框架的价值不在于少写几行代码,而在于把验证、存档、续训、日志这些工程项标准化;Lightning 藏循环、Ignite 露循环,选型取决于你想要的控制粒度。
357	
358	## 7. 下一步学习建议
359	
360	- 下一单元进入第 14 章(卷积神经网络):建议先读 [ch14/ch14_part1.py](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch14/ch14_part1.py) 中手写的 `conv1d`/`conv2d`,CNN 的训练循环仍可用本讲的三种方式书写——试着用 Lightning 改写 ch14 的训练代码是最好的巩固练习。
361	- 想深入 Lightning:对照阅读 `training_epoch_end` 在 Lightning 2.x 中的替代写法(`on_train_epoch_end` + `self.log(on_epoch=True)`),体会框架 API 演进对复现代码的影响。
362	- 想深入 Ignite:官方文档的 `Engine` 自定义 update 函数示例(不使用 `create_supervised_trainer`,直接 `Engine(step_fn)`)能帮你彻底看清「引擎只是循环 + 事件」这一本质。
363	- 建议把本讲的对比表扩展到 ch14 的 ResNet 微调场景:当模型更大、训练更久时,`ModelCheckpoint` 与断点续训的价值会远超本讲的小实验。

# 高层训练接口：PyTorch Lightning 与 Ignite

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲,你应该能够:

1. 说出「原始 PyTorch 训练循环」里的哪些活儿(双层 for 循环、`zero_grad`/`backward`/`step`、设备转移、指标累计、checkpoint 保存)被 Lightning 和 Ignite 分别接管了,哪些仍要你自己写。
2. 读懂 `MultiLayerPerceptron(pl.LightningModule)` 中 `training_step` / `validation_step` / `test_step` / `configure_optimizers` 四类方法的分工,理解「把训练逻辑收进类」这一设计。
3. 读懂 `MnistDataModule(pl.LightningDataModule)` 的 `prepare_data` / `setup` / 三个 `*_dataloader` 方法,理解「数据准备收进类」带来的复用与防泄漏好处。
4. 会用 `pl.Trainer(max_epochs=..., callbacks=..., gpus=...)`、`trainer.fit` / `trainer.test(ckpt_path='best')` 完成训练、测试与最佳模型挑选。
5. 理解 Ignite 的核心抽象:`Engine`(对循环的封装)+ `Events`(事件)+ handler(回调函数),会用 `create_supervised_trainer` / `create_supervised_evaluator` 搭一套带日志、checkpoint、TensorBoard 的训练流程。
6. 能横向对比同一 MNIST 任务在「原始 PyTorch / Lightning / Ignite」三种写法下的代码量与结构差异,并说出各自适合的场景。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲是第 13 章的收官,建立在前面几讲的基础上。先把几个概念用通俗语言说清楚:

- **训练循环的五步骨架**(u12-l3、u13-l2 已建立):对每个 batch 执行「前向算损失 → `loss.backward()` → `optimizer.step()` → `optimizer.zero_grad()`,外面包一层 epoch 循环」。这五步是所有框架要替你重复写的部分。
- **epoch 与 iteration**:一个 epoch 是把训练集完整过一遍;一个 iteration 是处理一个 batch。55000 个样本、batch_size=64 时,每个 epoch 约 860 个 iteration(859 个满批 + 1 个 24 样本的尾批,因为 `DataLoader` 默认 `drop_last=False`,见 u12-l2)。
- **样板代码(boilerplate)**:几乎每个项目都要抄一遍、但又不含任何「你的模型特有信息」的代码,比如把张量搬去 GPU、每个 epoch 结束时算一遍验证集、定期保存 checkpoint。高层接口的卖点就是把这些样板收走。
- **回调(callback)与事件(event)**:一种「好莱坞原则」的编程模式——别来调用框架,框架会调用你。你先把「某件事发生时该执行什么函数」注册好,框架运行到那个时点就替你调用。Ignite 里的 `Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED`(一个 epoch 结束)就是事件,你注册的函数就是 handler(处理器/回调)。
- **指标(metric)的累计式计算**(u11-l2 的 `compute_mse_and_acc` 已见过雏形):不能简单地对「每个 batch 的准确率」取平均——尾批只有 24 个样本,权重应当更小。正确做法是累计所有样本再整体计算:

\[ \text{Acc}=\frac{1}{\sum_b n_b}\sum_b \#\{i\in b:\hat{y}_i=y_i\} \quad\text{而非}\quad \frac{1}{B}\sum_b \text{acc}_b \]

  torchmetrics 的 `Accuracy` 就是「`update` 累计 → `compute` 总算 → `reset` 清零」的三段式。
- **checkpoint 与 state_dict**(u13-l2):存档里保存的是参数字典(以及优化器状态),用于断点续训和最佳模型恢复。本讲会看到两个框架如何把「定期保存、按验证指标挑最佳」自动化。
- **TensorBoard**:一个把标量(损失、准确率)随训练进程画成曲线的看板工具,`pip install tensorboard` 后用 `tensorboard --logdir=目录` 启动。

**版本提醒**:仓库代码基于 PyTorch Lightning 1.5.0、torchmetrics 0.6.2(见 [ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py:L36-L43](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L36-L43) 的版本检查字典)。若你安装的是 Lightning 2.x,`gpus=1`、`resume_from_checkpoint`、`training_epoch_end` 等 API 已有变动(后文相应处会标注),建议按 u1-l2 的方法建书配钉版本环境再跑。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py) | 用 PyTorch Lightning 训练 MNIST 多层感知机 | `MultiLayerPerceptron`、`MnistDataModule`、`Trainer` 的全部用法 |
| [ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py) | 用 PyTorch-Ignite 训练同一个 MNIST 模型 | `create_supervised_trainer/evaluator`、`Events` 回调、`Checkpoint`、`TensorboardLogger` |
| [ch13/ch13_part2.py](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part2.py) | 原始 PyTorch 写法的 MNIST 训练(对照基准) | L219-L280 的数据、模型与手写训练循环 |
| [ch13/ch13_part1.py](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part1.py) | 第 13 章前半部分:XOR 项目的通用 `train()` 函数(对照基准) | L281-L306 的双层循环与五步骨架 |

三个文件训练的是**同一个任务、几乎同一个模型**(Flatten → Linear(784,32) → ReLU → Linear(32,16) → ReLU → Linear(16,10)),正好构成一场控制变量实验:模型和数据不变,只变「训练代码的组织方式」。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 LightningModule:把训练逻辑收进类

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

u12-l3 和 u13-l2 里,模型只是 `nn.Module`(定义 `forward`),训练循环是一个独立的函数或脚本段落——模型与训练流程是分离的。Lightning 的第一个核心思想是:**把「一个 batch 的训练/验证/测试该怎么算」和「用哪个优化器」写成模型类的成员方法**,框架拿着这些方法去替你组装完整循环。

这样做的直接收益:

- 这些方法变成可复用、可单测的单元,换数据集、换 Trainer 配置都不用改;
- Lightning 通过方法名就能知道你的意图,从而自动决定何时 `model.train()` / `model.eval()`、何时关梯度、把设备转移、日志记录统一处理。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

Trainer 每个 iteration 大致执行(伪代码,标注「你写」/「框架代劳」):

```
for epoch in range(max_epochs):                     # 框架代劳
    for batch_idx, batch in enumerate(train_dl):    # 框架代劳
        loss = model.training_step(batch, batch_idx)  # 你写:前向 + 算损失 + 记指标
        loss.backward()                             # 框架代劳
        optimizer.step()                            # 框架代劳(优化器来自 configure_optimizers)
        optimizer.zero_grad()                       # 框架代劳
    model.training_epoch_end(outs)                  # 你写(旧版 API):整个 epoch 的指标汇总
```

对比 [ch13/ch13_part1.py:L287-L293](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part1.py#L287-L293) 中手写的同一段,你会发现 `training_step` 就是把五步骨架里「除了三行梯度代码」之外的部分抽成了方法。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

类的定义与构造:[ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py:L72-L97](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L72-L97) 定义 `MultiLayerPerceptron(pl.LightningModule)`。构造函数里做两件事:

`training_step`:[ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py:L103-L110](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L103-L110)

```python
def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
    x, y = batch
    logits = self(x)
    loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, y)
    preds = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)
    self.train_acc.update(preds, y)
    self.log("train_loss", loss, prog_bar=True)
    return loss
```

五个动作:解包 batch → 前向 → 算交叉熵损失 → 取 argmax 得预测 → 把 (预测, 标签) 喂给指标对象累计。`self.log("train_loss", loss, prog_bar=True)` 把当前损失登记到 Lightning 的日志系统并显示在进度条上;**返回值就是 loss,框架拿它去 `backward()`**。多分类输出层用交叉熵、输出层不套 Softmax(logits 进 `CrossEntropyLoss`),这与 u12-l3 讲的「输出层按任务匹配」一致。

`training_epoch_end`:[ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py:L112-L114](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L112-L114) 在整个 epoch 结束时调用 `self.train_acc.compute()` 得到按样本加权的整体准确率(见第 2 节公式),登记为 `"train_acc"`,再 `reset()` 清空累计、供下个 epoch 使用。**若用 Lightning 2.x,此方法已被移除**,替代做法是在 `self.log(...)` 中加 `on_epoch=True` 并改用 `on_train_epoch_end`。

`validation_step` / `validation_epoch_end`:[ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py:L116-L127](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L116-L127) 与训练版逐行对称,唯一差别是不做参数更新(框架已保证在 `no_grad` 与 `eval` 模式下执行)且记录的键名为 `"valid_loss"` / `"valid_acc"`。记住 `"valid_acc"` 这个键名——4.3 节的 ModelCheckpoint 靠它挑最佳模型。

`test_step`:[ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py:L129-L137](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L129-L137) 结构相同,小差异是它直接在 L136 每批之后 `compute()` 并登记 `test_acc`,没有单独的 epoch_end。

`configure_optimizers`:[ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py:L139-L141](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L139-L141) 返回 `torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=0.001)`,与 [ch13/ch13_part2.py:L258](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part2.py#L258) 完全一致——优化器的选择权始终在你手里。

2. **操作步骤**:打开 [ch13/ch13_part1.py:L282-L306](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part1.py#L282-L306) 的 `train()` 函数与 `training_step`,做一张左右对照表:内层循环的每一行对应 `training_step` 的哪一行、或被框架的哪项代劳(如 L291 `loss.backward()` → Trainer 代劳;L294 的 `loss_hist_train[epoch] += loss.item()` → `self.log` 代劳)。

4. **预期结果**:对照表中「框架代劳」应覆盖 backward / step / zero_grad / batch 转移设备 / epoch 边界管理五项;`training_step` 只保留「你的模型特有」的前向与损失定义。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**:为什么 `training_step` 里不写 `optimizer.zero_grad()`?
**答案**:`zero_grad`/`backward`/`step` 是所有模型都相同的骨架,由 Trainer 统一执行;`training_step` 只负责返回 loss。这也解释了 u12-l3 强调的「梯度是累加语义」在此处为何不再是隐患——清零由框架保证。

**练习 2**:如果去掉 `self.train_acc.reset()`([L114](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part3_lightning.py#L114)),第 2 个 epoch 登记的 `train_acc` 会是什么?
**答案**:前两个 epoch **全部样本**的整体准确率(累计未清空),数值会与第 1 个 epoch 的曲线不衔接,第 2 个 epoch 的「自身准确率」无法单独读出。

**练习 3**:三个 `Accuracy` 对象为什么分开建 `train_acc`/`valid_acc`/`test_acc`,而不是共用一个?
**答案**:metric 对象内部有累计状态;共用会让训练批的样本混进验证/测试指标,验证与测试就不再「干净」。分开建并各自 reset,保证三条曲线各自统计各自的样本。

### 4.2 LightningDataModule:数据准备也收进类

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

LightningModule 收编了「训练逻辑」,`LightningDataModule` 收编「数据逻辑」:下载、切分、变换、三个 DataLoader 的构造全部封装成一个可复用对象。好处有三:

1. **一处定义、处处复用**:fit / validate / test / predict 都从同一个对象取数,保证各阶段用的是同一套切分与变换;
2. **防数据泄漏的结构保障**:切分只发生在 `setup` 一处,且可以按 stage 区分,不会在笔记本里散落多处 `random_split`;
3. **多进程安全**:`prepare_data`(只在该进程执行一次的下载)与 `setup`(每个进程都要做的切分)分离,为分布式训练铺路。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```
实例化 mnist_dm = MnistDataModule()
trainer.fit(model, datamodule=mnist_dm)
 ├─ prepare_data()      # 下载 MNIST(只在主进程执行一次)
 ├─ setup('fit')        # 加载训练数据 → random_split 出 train/val → 存为 self.train/self.val
 ├─ train_dataloader()  # 每个阶段取各自的 DataLoader
 └─ val_dataloader()
trainer.test(..., datamodule=mnist_dm)
 └─ setup('test') 等价路径 → test_dataloader()
```

### 4.3 Trainer 与 ModelCheckpoint:一行 fit 背后的调度

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`pl.Trainer` 是 Lightning 的「总调度」:你把 LightningModule 和 DataModule 交给它,它负责循环、设备分配、日志聚合、进度条、checkpoint 回调、 TensorBoard 写入。你配置它的方式就是构造参数:`max_epochs`、`callbacks`、`gpus`(设备)等。这一节的重点是看清 **Trainer 参数、模块里的 `self.log` 键名、checkpoint 文件** 三者如何串成一条链。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```
callbacks = [ModelCheckpoint(save_top_k=1, mode='max', monitor="valid_acc")]
trainer = pl.Trainer(max_epochs=10, callbacks=callbacks)   # 有 GPU 时再加 gpus=1
trainer.fit(model, datamodule)          # 训练;每个 epoch 末用 valid_acc 挑最佳并存档
trainer.test(model, datamodule, ckpt_path='best')          # 加载验证准确率最高的存档测试
```

### 4.4 Ignite:用 Engine 保留循环、用回调拼装行为

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

Ignite 与 Lightning 的哲学不同。Lightning 把循环**藏起来**(你只写 step);Ignite 把循环**封装但保持可见**——核心类 `Engine` 接收一个「处理单个 batch 的函数」,替你跑双层循环并在各个时点触发事件,你再用回调把日志、验证、存档挂上去。书中源码注释([ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L70-L79](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L70-L79))总结为四件套:引擎与事件系统、开箱即用指标、内置 handlers、分布式支持。设计取向是「比纯 PyTorch 少写代码,但保留 PyTorch 式的完全控制」。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```
trainer = create_supervised_trainer(model, optimizer, loss_fn, device=device)   # 训练引擎
evaluator = create_supervised_evaluator(model, metrics={...}, device=device)    # 评估引擎
# 给 trainer 挂事件回调(日志、checkpoint)→ 给 evaluator 挂回调(验证指标、最佳模型)
trainer.run(train_loader, max_epochs=5)                                          # 一行启动
```

`create_supervised_trainer` 内部的循环等价于(伪代码):

```
while epoch < max_epochs:
    for batch in data:
        model.train(); x, y = move_to_device(batch)
        y_pred = model(x); loss = loss_fn(y_pred, y)
        optimizer.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); optimizer.step()
        触发 Events.ITERATION_COMPLETED(把 loss 存进 trainer.state.output)
    触发 Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED
触发 Events.COMPLETED
```

也就是 u12-l3 的五步骨架原封不动,只是由引擎执行、并在固定时点发事件。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

### 4.5 Ignite 的 Events 事件系统与 handlers

#### 4.5.1 概念说明

`Engine` 在固定时点触发事件(事件是一个枚举 `Events`,如 `ITERATION_COMPLETED`、`EPOCH_COMPLETED`、`COMPLETED`),你把普通 Python 函数挂到事件上,它们就成了回调。挂接有两种等价写法:**装饰器** `@trainer.on(Events.XXX)` 与显式调用 `trainer.add_event_handler(Events.XXX, fn)`。此外 Ignite 内置了一类现成回调——handlers,如 `Checkpoint`(存档)、`DiskSaver`(写磁盘)、`TensorboardLogger`(写 TensorBoard),直接拿来挂即可,不必自己写函数。

#### 4.5.2 核心流程

```
@trainer.on(Events.ITERATION_COMPLETED(every=100))   # 带过滤器:每 100 个 iteration
def log_training_loss(): ...                          # 打印 trainer.state.output 里的 batch 损失

@trainer.on(Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED)                   # 每个 epoch 结束
def log_validation_results():
    evaluator.run(val_loader)                          # 跑评估引擎 → 读 state.metrics

trainer.add_event_handler(Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED, checkpoint_handler)   # 每 epoch 存档
evaluator.add_event_handler(Events.COMPLETED, best_model_handler)       # 每次评估后按准确率存最佳
tb_logger.attach_output_handler(...)                  # 指标写入 TensorBoard
```

`trainer.state` 是引擎的「仪表盘」:`state.epoch`、`state.max_epochs`、`state.iteration`、`state.output`(当前 batch 的损失)在回调里随取随用。

#### 4.5.3 源码精读

训练日志回调:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L193-L202](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L193-L202)。`Events.ITERATION_COMPLETED(every=log_interval)` 是「事件 + 过滤器」的组合,`log_interval=100` 意味着并非每个 batch 都打印(否则 938 个 iteration/epoch 会刷屏);函数体从 `trainer.state` 取 epoch、iteration 和当前批损失并格式化打印。

验证回调:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L212-L220](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L212-L220)。挂在 **trainer** 的 `EPOCH_COMPLETED` 上,函数体却去 `evaluator.run(val_loader)`——「训练引擎的 epoch 结束」触发「评估引擎完整跑一遍验证集」,这是两个 Engine 协作的典型写法;`eval_state.metrics['accuracy']` 与 `['loss']` 正是 4.4 建指标表时自定义的键名。

每 epoch 存档:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L230-L242](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L230-L242)。`to_save = {"model": model, "optimizer": optimizer, "trainer": trainer}` 说明存档内容不止模型参数(与 u13-l2 的 checkpoint 概念对齐:含优化器状态才能严格续训);`DiskSaver(dirname="./output", require_empty=False)` 负责写盘;`Checkpoint(to_save, save_handler, filename_prefix="training")` 组装后用**显式** `trainer.add_event_handler(Events.EPOCH_COMPLETED, checkpoint_handler)` 挂上——源码注释 L205 特意说明这与装饰器写法等价。

按验证准确率存最佳模型:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L253-L263](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L253-L263)。又一个 `Checkpoint`,但 `n_saved=1`、`score_name="accuracy"`、`score_function=Checkpoint.get_default_score_fn("accuracy")`(从 evaluator 的指标表里取 accuracy 打分),并且挂在 **evaluator** 的 `COMPLETED` 上——每次评估完就「以准确率为分数」覆盖式保存,与 Lightning `ModelCheckpoint(monitor="valid_acc", mode='max', save_top_k=1)` 目的相同,只是这里需要你亲手接线。

TensorBoard 日志:[ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py:L266-L291](https://github.com/rasbt/machine-learning-book/blob/63bee951ca45420ac33ccf803ceb337afc3c0a91/ch13/ch13_part4_ignite.py#L266-L291)。`TensorboardLogger(log_dir=output_path)` 之后调用两次 `attach_output_handler`:一次挂 trainer 的 `ITERATION_COMPLETED(every=100)` 写批损失(`output_transform=lambda loss: {"batch_loss": loss}` 把引擎输出变换为要记录的字典),一次挂 evaluator 的 `EPOCH_COMPLETED` 写全部指标(`metric_names="all"`),`global_step_transform=global_step_from_engine(trainer)` 让验证曲线的横坐标对齐训练引擎的全局步数而非评估引擎自己的步数——否则两条曲线在 TensorBoard 里对不齐。启动看板:`tensorboard --logdir='./output'`(源码注释 L303-L305)。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `LightningModule` 把「单 batch 的训练/验证/测试怎么算」(`training_step` / `validation_step` / `test_step`)和「用哪个优化器」(`configure_optimizers`)收进模型类,梯度三件套(backward/step/zero_grad)全部交给 Trainer。
- torchmetrics 指标对象用 `update → compute → reset` 三段式累计,epoch 末得到的是按样本数加权的整体准确率,而非批准确率的平均。
- `LightningDataModule` 用 `prepare_data`(下载一次)/ `setup`(切分)/ 三个 `*_dataloader` 统一数据准备;它是三种实现中唯一真正切出 5000 张验证集的版本。
- `ModelCheckpoint(monitor="valid_acc", mode='max', save_top_k=1)` 与 `self.log` 的键名构成隐式契约;`trainer.test(ckpt_path='best')` 自动加载验证集上最优的存档。
- Ignite 的核心是 `Engine` + `Events`:循环被封装但仍可见,日志、验证、checkpoint、TensorBoard 全部以回调/ handler 的形式挂接到具体事件上,`trainer.run(data, max_epochs=5)` 一行启动。
- 框架的价值不在于少写几行代码,而在于把验证、存档、续训、日志这些工程项标准化;Lightning 藏循环、Ignite 露循环,选型取决于你想要的控制粒度。

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

  }

  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
